newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Capital Intelligence reaffirms ICICI, SCICI rating.
newsitem.headline: Capital Intelligence reaffirms ICICI, SCICI rating.

text.p: Capital Intelligence has reaffirmed its ratings for Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India and SCICI Ltd, the specialist bank rating agency said on Thursday.
Both institutions carry ratings of BBB+ long term and A-2 short term with a stable outlook, the Cyprus-based agency said.
There has been a proposed merger between the two Indian development institutions. The merged institution will bear the name of ICICI, and SCICI will cease to exist as a separate entity.

Once the merger becomes effective, expected by March 1997, ICICI's ratings will be maintained, but will be reviewed on the basis of new financials for the merged institution, Capital Intelligence said.

SCICI, originally known as Shipping Credit and Investment Corporation of India Ltd, was established in 1986 on the initiative of ICICI, which retains a 17 percent shareholding. It enjoys solid capitalisation, good profitability and superior asset quality. SCICI, which had total assets of US$2 billion at end September 1996, is a major provider of credit to the shipping industry, but since 1991 has diversified its portfolio to include all sectors of the economy.
Established in 1955, ICICI, which is majority owned by state run institutions, is the second largest development bank in the country, with total assets of US$ 7.7 billion at end September 1996.

It has strong financials and has performed consistently well in recent years. ICICI's capitalisation will improve after the merger, as SCICI was less highly leveraged. Proforma accounts for the combined institution as at end September 1996 show a capital adequacy ratio of 13.1 percent, 0.7 percent higher than that of ICICI alone at the same date.

ICICI will thus have more scope for asset expansion without the need to raise fresh capital. The merger also prepares the ground for ICICI'S increased participation in lending to the growing Indian infrastructure sector which requires large investments.
Generally the implications of the merger for the credit standing of the new institution are considered to be favourable, Capital Intelligence said.
